long-term exposure to traffic-related air pollution is associated with an increased risk of stroke.

the health effects of traffic-related air pollution.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no conclusive evidence of an association of air pollution exposure with the risk of stroke.
we did not find evidence of an association, but the possibility of a true association cannot be excluded.
there is suggestive evidence of an effect of NOx and PM10, but the evidence is not strong enough to draw a firm conclusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there was a weak but statistically significant increase in stroke with increased NOX and PM 10 exposure.
we have not found evidence of an increased stroke risk related to long-term exposure to local traffic-related air pollution.
the risk of stroke is increased with increasing long-term exposure to air pollution, but there is no clear evidence of a threshold level of exposure.

the risk of stroke associated with long-term exposure to traffic-related air pollution seems to be present even at relatively low concentrations.
there is a need for more epidemiological evidence on the role of traffic pollution in stroke, especially in the general population.
